title: biographical introduction; train journey to Idaho
description: The interview opens with background on Myrtle Berg's birth and her arrival in Idaho from North Carolina in 1952. She recounts the slow train ride to Cincinnati and the segregation and eventual integration she experienced. She also discusses her mother's name and birthplace.

title: family home; mother's factory piecework
description: Berg describes growing up in North Carolina and her mother carrying shoe piecework home from a factory. She explains that the children, especially girls, were expected to contribute this piecework after school.

title: father's work roles; shifting gender expectations
description: The conversation shifts to the father, who was often semi-retired and doing household tasks while the mother entered plant work full-time. Berg contrasts how this arrangement seemed then and now, with the family unwillingly holding to conventional gender roles.

title: frequent moves; parents' work patterns
description: Berg speaks about her father's tendency to try new ventures, including homesteading and clearing land, leading the family to move often. She notes that her father held various construction and factory jobs while her mother stayed home and later worked.

title: parents' details; father's occupations
description: She provides details about her father William Alfonso Berg and his work history, including road projects and factory work. She helps sort birth and death dates and remembers siblings who passed away.

title: marriage; children; education
description: Berg discusses her husband, their marriage in 1952, and introduces their three children with their ages. She describes her own education, a BS in education from the University of Idaho, and her teaching role.

title: teaching and part-time jobs; piecework memories
description: Berg lists previous jobs in cafeterias, secretarial work and part-time teaching. She revisits the shoe piecework more fully, describing family labor roles and her regret that she had little time for recreation.

title: returning to college; being an older female student
description: She explains how financial necessity and her desire to teach led her back to college as an older woman while raising her family. She describes commuting to classes, studying with young classmates, and receiving varied reactions from teachers and students.

title: children's education choices
description: Berg talks about her daughter delaying formal education to work and her son exploring drama while undecided about declaring a major, noting his intensive involvement in a recent play.

title: daughter's marriage views; leisure pursuits
description: She indicates she does not pressure her daughter about marriage and is supportive of her social life, though she hopes for thoughtful timing. She ends with details about teaching Cub Scouts, Girl Scouts, and enjoying dining, film, and personal time with her husband.

title: Camping life; husband's heart attack and retreat to countryside
description: Myrtle Berg discusses her family's camping trips, explaining how they graduated from tents to a camper trailer parked by the riverbank. She reveals her husband suffered a heart attack due to overwork, prompting these retreats to the river for relaxation and escape from home projects.

title: Small town advantages; Depression and wartime poverty
description: The conversation turns to the benefits of rural living versus big city life, particularly the open spaces for children to play. Isabel Miller asks about the Depression era, and Myrtle explains how wartime poverty and low factory wages shaped her family's financial caution, making them fearful of spending and debt.

title: Gardening and preserving; family size
description: Myrtle discusses attempting to garden and preserve food, including an early mishap where apple jelly overflowed in a copper kettle. The topic shifts to family size and birth control, with Myrtle describing her mother's eleven children, the struggle for survival, and the subtle messages she received about limiting family size.

title: War service; marriage and finishing school
description: Myrtle describes her brothers' service in the Army and Navy during World War II, war bonds, and her sister's wartime work. She then recounts meeting her husband, marrying in Kellogg, moving to Minnesota during the Korean War, and finishing high school while married and pregnant, noting she was the only married student in her school.

title: Marital decision making; financial roles
description: The interview concludes with an extended discussion of how Myrtle and her husband make decisions together, contrasting their partnership with friends who have more traditional arrangements. She reflects on women's financial independence, her mother's lack of control, and how they include their children in discussions about money and family decisions.
